correctness.rationale: Every closed neighborhood is either a leaf singleton plus its internal ancestor chain or an internal singleton plus its descendant-leaf cluster. The exhaustive support classification is proved, the closed-form coefficients follow from depth summation, and a depth-h adaptive tree meets the h-bit counting upper bound. The chordal-bipartite and diameter-four claims have graph-theoretic proofs. Finite exhaustive traces and exact rank recursion independently reproduce all specified small cases; no finite observation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary graph-VC literature treats closed neighborhoods in full generality, while the accessible comparisons do not imply the exact three-coefficient profile, its LCA classification, and its simultaneous sharp online rank on these ancestor-incidence graphs. The prefix online tree is standard; the contribution is the exact integrated graph-family profile. Searches cannot establish exhaustive historical priority, which remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Potential exact finite ancestor-incidence/laminar-system enumeration may exist under other names; search cannot rule this out.
Some plausible background sources were only abstract- or partial-text-inspected; none supplied a decisive contrary exact theorem in accessible material.
The binary prefix strategy as an online lower bound is classical; priority is claimed only for the integrated finite graph profile and exact full description.

value.rationale: The exact polynomial is a complete natural invariant for a two-sided closed-neighborhood system on an infinite, geometrically restricted graph family. It gives a full classification and count of maximal shattered supports, identifies a sharp growing adaptive-static gap while VC remains three, and achieves the entropy upper bound despite diameter four and chordal bipartiteness; these quantified structural facts are not a mere normalization check.
